steps.name: Runner records the guest's view once and retains every replicate's console
steps.description: Replicate::report_guest_view and Replicate::retain_console, RecordSink::write_artifact (create-new, creates parents), and the runner behaviour for a guest benchmark per DDD-2, DDD-4, DDD-9 and the runner rule M-1; .gitignore gains benchmarks/results/**/artifacts/.
steps.implementation_notes: @sizing-review-needed Scenario count 16 (GR1-GR16; GR13 is a green guard). Exact contract: feature-delta DDD-4 (report_guest_view: first call fixes the run's view and the runner appends the one guest_observed line before that replicate's line; later calls return Ok and change nothing; a native benchmark calling it is a ReplicateFailure; under smoke only the effect is skipped and every failure rule applies as in a real run), DDD-9 (retain_console writes artifacts/<profile>/<block>-<position>-<arm>/console.log create-new; a second call or a write failure is a ReplicateFailure) and the DDD-2 wiring order (the runner maps substrate 'guest' to Substrate::Guest, writes the static guest block on run_started including on a refused host, never calls the family body when the host is refused, fails a guest-substrate replicate that returned Ok without reporting a view with reason 'the replicate reported no guest view'). No guest port and no new dependency in overdrive-bench (ADR-0331). Replace the DISTILL scaffolds (inert Ok(())). CONSOLE-RETENTION GITIGNORE: add `benchmarks/results/**/artifacts/` to .gitignore in this step (approved with PD-9); the record and report stay committed, the consoles are not. GR12 is a proptest over scripted replicate sequences (seed printed on failure). Do not weaken any body.
criteria: GR1-GR12 and GR14-GR16 pass with should_panic removed; GR13 stays green

A guest benchmark's record is: run_started with substrate guest and the static guest block, then (after the start canary) one guest_observed line holding the FIRST reported view immediately before that replicate's line, later views change nothing, a view reported by a replicate that then fails stays the run's view; the record validates in every script

A guest-substrate replicate returning Ok without a view is failed 'the replicate reported no guest view' (also under smoke); a drifted host writes exactly run_started (with the guest block) and run_refused and never calls the body; a native benchmark that reports a view fails its replicate

Every replicate's console lands at artifacts/<profile>/<block>-<position>-<arm>/console.log under the result directory in every outcome, create-new; a second retain_console or a failed artifact write fails the replicate and the run continues; FileSink::write_artifact writes bytes and parents and a second write is AlreadyExists with the first bytes kept

steps.name: Guest program return is printed and parsed under one strict console grammar
steps.description: print_program_return and parse_program_return in overdrive_testing::guest_app: the leading newline, two guest-reading lines, one framed forwarded_round_trip_ns series block of at most 16 values per line, and a SHA-256 end line over little-endian u64 bytes; the parser matches begin and reading lines only at the start of a console line and accepts exactly one intact block of the expected count (DDD-6).
steps.implementation_notes: @sizing-review-needed Scenario count 17 (GA1-GA17). Exact contract: feature-delta DDD-6 (output grammar, GuestReading, ProgramReturn, ProgramReturnError, parse_program_return); the printer sits beside the parser so one owner holds the grammar (U1). LEADING NEWLINE IS LOAD-BEARING: the printer writes one '\n' BEFORE the two reading lines and the series block, because overdrive-init writes unterminated log fragments to the shared console and a first line glued to one is lost (findings-production-init-return.md: 24 of 60 replicates lost the block without the newline, 0 of 30 with it; ADR-0330 states why a tolerant begin match is rejected). No drain, flush or sleep is needed or added. The end line carries the metric and checksum only; the count is not printed. SHARED-CONTROL ACTIVATION GROUP: GA6, GA7, GA10, GA11 and GA17 assert only Err/BlockMissing and are satisfied by the always-Err scaffold for the wrong reason, so they activate TOGETHER with the first parser that parses an intact console. Procedure: remove ALL should_panic markers of GA6, GA7, GA10, GA11, GA17, run each body once against the minimal implementation, expect the semantic RED of every rule not yet implemented, route ANY body defect to the acceptance designer (do NOT weaken or rewrite a body), then continue one test at a time. The variant for a begin line without an end line, a non-numeric value or a spliced line is crafter detail (U2); GA16 accepts CountMismatch or ChecksumMismatch for a dropped value. sha2 is already a workspace dependency of overdrive-testing. Add unit and proptest coverage for crafter helpers; GA15 and GA16 are proptests (seed printed on failure).
criteria: GA1-GA17 pass with should_panic removed; the five shared-control tests GA6, GA7, GA10, GA11, GA17 were activated together, each body run once against a minimal implementation, any body defect routed back to the acceptance designer and none weakened

An intact console parses to its two readings (text, absent:<reason>, unreadable:<error>) and its values in order, through kernel lines and an unterminated overdrive-init fragment ended by the program's leading newline; glued to the fragment the first reading is ReadingMissing naming kernel

Every damaged return is refused and never shortened: no begin line BlockMissing, two blocks BlockRepeated, count mismatch CountMismatch{expected,found} with a Display naming both numbers, changed value ChecksumMismatch, missing or repeated reading naming its key, a reading line without '=' is Err; for every non-empty u64 series print then parse returns exactly what was printed (GA15) and a damaged block never parses to a different series (GA16)
The checksum is the SHA-256 of the values as consecutive little-endian u64 bytes and the fixed vectors of GA3 pass

steps.name: A guest program run reports its exit and console in every outcome and leaves no VMM
steps.description: The real run_in_guest_program and ProgramRun per DDD-5/DDD-6: boots a production-init guest, plays the node beacon, runs the program as the operator command after loading the vsock loopback module, waits for EXIT within the bound, ends the guest and reaps the VMM in every outcome; GuestImageSpec::benchmark() carries the loopback module; run_in_guest_cell shares the body and reads the two shape constants.
steps.implementation_notes: Scenario count 7 (GF1-GF6, GK3). Exact contract: feature-delta 'DDD-5 and DDD-6' signatures (run_in_guest_program, ProgramRun, LANE_GUEST_VCPUS, LANE_GUEST_MEMORY_MIB, GuestImageSpec::benchmark) and G-2. run_in_guest_cell keeps its behaviour and shares its body with run_in_guest_program; the lane's inline 512 and 2 become the two constants both read. Postconditions: the VMM has exited and been reaped before return in EVERY outcome; the console is complete only when the VMM exited on its own after EXIT; a VMM still running after the post-EXIT wait makes exit an Err (the wait result is NEVER discarded); the outer Err is only for failure before a VMM exists. THE EXIT BOUND IS MEASURED FROM THE EXEC WRITE exactly as run_in_guest_cell does (GF4). GuestImageSpec::benchmark() must equal the pinned literal (OverdriveInit, forwarder_module, loopback_module, no extra files; GK3) or every program exits 65. GF1-GF6 use benchmark-band CID slots 10-15, one per case, each in its own cgroup-default nested-launch outer guest; the REGISTERED band count stays six. Whenever the guest peer binary changes, rerun `cargo xtask metal run -- cargo xtask guest-kit-prepare` before the Metal tests (the scripted-init seam GF6 uses is already in bin/guest_peer.rs). Remove the six should_panic markers and GK3's; do not write, replace or weaken any body; a missing fixture or oracle routes back to the acceptance designer. Do not add API beyond the DDD-5/6 signatures.
criteria: GF1-GF6 and GK3 pass with should_panic removed: no READY, a guest stalled past READY_BOUND, death after READY, a missed EXIT bound (bound counted from the EXEC write), a VMM that outlives its guest's EXIT, and the clean-exit control each report the pinned exit Ok/Err, the retained console, a reaped VMM (no vhost-vsock holder, no /proc/<pid>) and a CID that boots the next guest
GuestImageSpec::benchmark() equals production init with forwarder_module true, loopback_module true and no extra files, and differs from workload()
run_in_guest_cell behaviour is unchanged: the existing in-guest lane tests still pass, and the lane reads LANE_GUEST_VCPUS and LANE_GUEST_MEMORY_MIB instead of the inline 2 and 512

steps.name: The guest flow forwarding family runs in a fresh guest per replicate with its smoke test
steps.description: Family guest-flow-forwarding (benchmark guest_flow_forwarding) per DDD-8: the forwarding-bench guest-peer subcommand drives the production guest flow owner through its vsock wire seam and prints the readings and the series block; the family host half boots one fresh guest per replicate, parses the return, reports the guest view and records one series metric forwarded_round_trip_ns; the declaration and its macro-generated smoke test land together.
steps.implementation_notes: Scenario count 1 generated smoke plus four native smokes plus crafter-owned unit tests. Exact contract: feature-delta DDD-8 (declaration: family guest-flow-forwarding, substrate guest, arms [forwarding], replicates 30, ONE metric forwarded_round_trip_ns unit ns table forwarded-path series, clock(guest = guest_monotonic), smoke(guest = "cgroup-default", profile = "nested-launch"); NO bpf_stats, NO reference, no A/A), DDD-5/DDD-6 (per-replicate order and failure reasons), DDD-10 (no new staging) and ADR-0332. The program is a subcommand of the existing overdrive-guest-peer (forwarding-bench): confirm where subcommands register (guest_app.rs, src/guest_peer.rs, bin/guest_peer.rs) and touch only what is needed; no prepare step, no GuestFile, no new bin; after ANY change to the peer rerun `cargo xtask metal run -- cargo xtask guest-kit-prepare`. W = 200 unrecorded, R = 5,000 timed 64-byte closed-loop round trips; the program prints through the step 01-06 printer (leading newline first) and exits non-zero when a flow cannot be driven; no failure is printed as a series line. Host half: artifact SHA-256 digests (init_bin, peer_bin, forwarder_module) computed ONCE per run; CID = GUEST_BENCHMARK.cid(n) with n a family-private counter of replicates this process started, modulo the band width 16 (the first replicate of the run, then wrap at replicate 17); workload address and launch token derived from lane_workload_addr(cid) and LANE_LAUNCH_TOKEN as the in-guest lane does; GuestView.vcpus/memory_mib from LANE_GUEST_VCPUS/LANE_GUEST_MEMORY_MIB; retain_console in every outcome that produced a console; every failure is Err(ReplicateFailure::fixture(..)), never a metric failure returned Ok. CRAFTER-OWNED UNIT COVERAGE (test-scenarios.md): the replicate counter modulo 16 that picks the CID; artifact digests computed once per run; the mapping of each ProgramReturnError to `the guest returned no intact readings: <cause>` or `the guest returned no intact forwarded_round_trip_ns block: <cause>`; the argv of forwarding-bench; GuestKitError::LaneNotPrepared mapping to the replicate failure `guest boot: <cause>` with the cause naming `cargo xtask guest-kit-prepare` (an unprepared kit fails every replicate before any guest launches, CA-4); a non-zero exit mapping to `the in-guest program exited <n>`; an outer Err mapping to `guest boot: <cause>`; exit Err mapping to `guest run: <cause>`. The family declaration and its generated smoke test MUST land in this ONE step; nothing in nextest proves the family before it. The docs (catalogue row, methodology section) are written in 03-02 with the measured figures.
criteria: The family declaration builds and its macro-generated smoke test (smoke_guest_flow_forwarding or the name the macro generates) passes in the cgroup-default nested-launch guest after one replicate per arm with no timing assertion; the four native smoke tests (cgroup-connect-hook, dns-responder, mtls-path, vm-lifecycle) pass unchanged

Crafter-owned unit tests pass: LaneNotPrepared becomes the replicate failure `guest boot: <cause>` naming `cargo xtask guest-kit-prepare` with no guest launched; a non-zero program exit becomes `the in-guest program exited <n>`; each ProgramReturnError maps to its pinned failure text; the replicate counter wraps modulo 16 onto GUEST_BENCHMARK.cid; artifact digests are computed once per run
A broken or missing series block makes the smoke test fail naming the benchmark (the replicate fails with the pinned reason and smoke panics), never passes over a guest that returned nothing
The family never launches the overdrive or benchmark binary and declares no bpf_stats and no reference

steps.name: Retained run E-G1 and host-drift refusal E-G2, with the measured cycle figures V-D
steps.description: ORCHESTRATOR-CAPTURED EVIDENCE, not a crafter TDD step: the walking skeleton run through cargo xtask metal run --benchmark guest-flow-forwarding on the exclusive Metal host, the K3 drift refusal, and the V-D reporting figures; reviewed by a different agent.
steps.implementation_notes: EVIDENCE, NOT A TEST (.claude/rules/testing.md classification; verification.md): no code is written; the orchestrator captures, a different agent audits ('different fox'); narrated evidence is rejected. If a capture exposes a defect it returns to the owning code step, not patched here. Prerequisites at the measured commit: bpf-build, kmod-build, `cargo xtask metal run -- cargo xtask guest-kit-prepare`, `cargo xtask metal run --exclusive -- cargo xtask kmod-load`; raise OVERDRIVE_METAL_LEASE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS if admission starves. Consoles under artifacts/ stay uncommitted (.gitignore from 01-04). Evidence is pinned to its SHA and substrate; record uname -r. V-D figures (feed the catalogue row in 03-02): the metric's median and spread across replicates, the per-replicate cycle (launch to EXIT) and console-return time, the failed-replicate rate (prior measurement ~2.75 s per replicate, ~83 s per 30). E-G5 (CID reuse at replicate 17) is observed in this same 30-replicate run.
